Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification (white-out) of the left hemithorax with a distinct mediastinal shift to the right (contralateral side), which is the classic radiographic presentation of a massive pleural effusion acting as a space-occupying lesion. While tension pneumothorax also causes a contralateral shift, it presents with hyperlucency (blackness) rather than opacification, and atelectasis would cause an ipsilateral shift.
